payload.blocks: Only the `config patch` verb for the confined supervisor head (p-vquz26ibnn item 2). friction record and the lead's supervisor raise land now; lead:SUPERVISOR keeps applying config patches by hand meanwhile.
payload.headline: How should a confined supervisor's `config patch` be held to the project config file only?

parts.cause: The host decides the destination file per key (packages/config/rust/src/provider/unix_verbs.rs) and has no switch to refuse anything but the project file; config's own confined-write guard never fires because the socket route runs unconfined.

options.cost: One small unit plus a footprint widening by the supervisor.
options.does: Add a `--project-only` flag to the host's `config patch` that refuses any item whose destination is not the project file; the socket route always passes it, sends the items inline and writes them to a private file the head cannot touch. Needs packages/config/rust added to this plan's footprint.
options.gain: One authority decides; no JS copy to drift; closes all three bypasses.
options.harm: One new host flag (RUL104: a contract addition).
options.label: Host --project-only switch

options.does: The route accepts only plain dotted keys and [N] indexes, reads the schema markers, fails closed, and writes inline items to a private file.
options.harm: A second copy of the host's destination rule that can drift (design principle 7).
options.label: Strict-grammar route guard

options.does: The confined supervisor never patches config; lead:SUPERVISOR or the owner applies patches by hand, as now.
options.harm: p-vquz26ibnn item 2 stays open; config steps keep needing a manual session.
options.label: Drop the verb

parts.recommendation: Host --project-only switch: the host already owns the destination decision, so the only safe fence is in the host.

scope.allows: One host flag on config patch that refuses non-project destinations, the socket route passing it with inline items, and widening this plan's footprint to the config crate for that.
scope.forbids: Letting a confined head reach global or accounts config by any path, or any other config door change.

parts.what: Phase 2 added `config patch` to the supervisor's socket grant (owner yes 2026-11-21). Review found that through the socket the host runs outside the sandbox and picks the destination file per key, so a head can write ~/.fgos/config.yaml or the accounts file. A route-side guard (a JS copy of the host's key resolution) was bypassed three ways: bracket paths like runner["llmAccounts"], swapping the patch file between the two reads, and symlinks. The verb is taken out of phase 2 until you pick.
